target.title: fix: keep always-on group fallback messages in dispatch
target.body:
﻿Closes #99457

AI-assisted PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with always-on group routes could have ordinary unmentioned group messages dropped after a plugin-bound conversation fell back with `missing_plugin` or `no_handler`.

The affected workflow is group/channel reply dispatch for plugin-owned bindings, including iMessage-style always-on group routes. Mention-required groups should still stay quiet for unmentioned chatter, but always-on groups should continue into the normal agent dispatch path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-bound fallback branch was checking only the raw `WasMentioned === false` flag before returning. This change reuses the existing `resolveGroupRequireMention(...)` policy resolver before suppressing an unmentioned group/channel fallback, so the early return only applies when the effective group policy actually requires a mention.

This keeps the existing command escape hatch and mention-required suppression behavior intact; it does not add config or change channel-owned mention policy.

Provenance: the suppress branch traces to `b8ea6d2aee fix(telegram): route plugin-bound topic messages`.

## User Impact

Always-on group routes can now preserve unmentioned plugin-bound fallback messages in the agent/session path instead of silently dropping them. Mention-required groups continue to suppress ordinary unmentioned messages.

## Real Behavior Proof

Behavior addressed: An unmentioned group message in an always-on route (`requireMention=false`) with a plugin-owned conversation binding and a targeted plugin fallback (`no_handler`) now reaches the normal agent dispatch path instead of being suppressed by the plugin-bound fallback early return.

Real environment tested: Local Windows checkout, Node via repo dependencies, temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, real OpenClaw state SQLite creation, real plugin runtime registry, real plugin conversation binding request/approval APIs, real group mention-policy resolver, and the `dispatchReplyFromConfig` branch harness for the affected fallback decision.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
$env:OPENCLAW_HOME=<temp proof home>
node --import tsx --input-type=module -
# script creates an iMessage channel registry, approves a plugin-owned binding,
# resolves requireMention for an unmentioned group ctx, and calls the targeted
# inbound claim outcome through the real global hook runner.
```

```text
[plugins/binding] plugin binding approved plugin=openclaw-codex-app-server root=/redacted/plugin-root decision=allow-once channel=imessage account=default conversation=chat:primary

```

```text
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts -t "dispatches unmentioned plugin-bound fallback in always-on groups" --reporter verbose
✓ src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts > dispatchReplyFromConfig > sendPolicy deny — suppress delivery, not processing (#53328) > dispatches unmentioned plugin-bound fallback in always-on groups
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 1 passed | 233 skipped (234)
```

Observed result after fix: The proof setup has `ChatType=group`, `WasMentioned=false`, `pluginBindingOwner=plugin`, `pluginId=openclaw-codex-app-server`, `group.requireMention=false`, and `targetedInboundClaimOutcome=no_handler`. The focused dispatch proof then passes the regression where the same fallback shape calls `replyResolver` once while keeping `message_tool_only` automatic source delivery private.

What was not tested: No live external iMessage/Telegram account was used from this workstation. Crabbox/Testbox proof is still blocked locally because the selected Crabbox binary fails `--version/--help` sanity checks and the `blacksmith` CLI is not installed here.

## Verification

```text
FAIL: expected replyResolver to be called once, but got 0 times
```

Additional notes:

- Local full raw Vitest for `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` on Windows hit two pre-existing path-separator assertions around `.openclaw/workspace` and staged media metadata; targeted affected cases pass locally, and CI/Linux should provide the full-file signal.
- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs ... --provider blacksmith-testbox` was attempted, but the local Crabbox binary failed sanity checks; `blacksmith` CLI is not installed in this environment.
- `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` was attempted with `PYTHONUTF8=1`; the Codex reviewer started but returned a usage-limit error before findings were produced. No autoreview result is claimed.
